name: Runner Tests Fixture - Session User Row Name Collision
brief: #2983: a User row carrying the session user's NAME under a different security id is ADOPTED by the session, not refused. Measured, not assumed.
description: The #2941 review predicted that a --test-data backup containing its own TESTUSER would collide with the runner's session-user seed. This fixture arranges exactly that collision -- its Install codeunit writes a different security id under the session user's own user name, and Install triggers run ahead of EnsureUserSystemTableRowSeeded. Real BC refuses a duplicate user name from a TRIGGER, not an index: SystemTableTriggers.OnBeforeInsertAsync's case 2000000120: arm validates a unique user name before writing, and AlRunner/Patches/UserTableTriggerPatches.cs reproduces that (#2983), so the seed cannot write its own row here. What it does instead is a maintainer decision of 2026-09-06: it ADOPTS this row's security id as the session's own, so UserSecurityId() returns {A17E9C42-5B08-4D6F-9E31-0C7A2F84B155} rather than the runner-generated {C0A1BDFA-0000-0000-0000-545553545553}. That makes UserSecurityId() depend on the contents of a backup file, so every adoption is reported on stderr at [warn] naming the user, the id taken and the id it replaced. The sibling fixture SessionUserRowAlreadyPresent asserts the other concrete value, which is what stops a constant-returning implementation satisfying both.
